doc.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
doc.interviewee: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack")

title: Songs Mary sang and Billy wrote
summary: Mary sang plain blues and Easy Rider, learned in Memphis. Billy mentions his Oh Me, Oh My Blues and My Heartbreaking Gal, and that Henry Williams took their material.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I was going to ask about when you would sing with the Oliver Band, can you remember some of the other songs? You mentioned the Royal Garden Blues. I know it's hard to remember all those titles, but what type of songs did you...
Oh, I just sing the blues, you know, plain blues, and Easy Rider, because, you see, I learned all those numbers at Hande's in the Memphis.
You'd sing some songs that I wrote too, like the... Oh Me, Oh My blues now. Oh, yes. That's something I wrote about 50 years ago, which I probably said, oh, record it.
Oh, we had plenty of songs on the ground.
I've heard of that. Didn't somebody else record that? Somebody made a record. Henry Williams, he took lots of our... It must have been Henry Williams. Rubberlegs.
He took lots of our music, because he worked with our show, see. I've seen that title.
Uh-huh. Uh-huh. And there was My Heartbreaking Gal, a song of mine.
